chunks: He, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, also forbade irfa’, and that is much smearing of (liquid) substances (on the body).

key_terms.الْإِرْفَاءِ: Excessive smearing or application of liquid substances/ointments on the body
key_terms.صَلَى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his Family (SAWW)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'irfa' in Shia hadith and what practice does it forbid?
ai.summary: In *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records the Prophet’s prohibition of *al-irfa’*, defined as the excessive application of perfumes or ointments, which was a pre-Islamic practice associated with vanity and ostentatious display of wealth. This ruling aligns with the broader Shia jurisprudential emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) and the rejection of *israf* (extravagance) in personal adornment, distinguishing between permissible beautification and excessive indulgence.
